answer: At every epoch, a random subset audits identities; fake agents multiply cost without reaching the reputation zenith, since their bond is slashed on failed attestation. Sybil resistance can be grounded in a stake-and-reputation inlet: each agent must lock a bond proportional to its claimed influence, and reputation only accrues through attested peer work. This keeps the economy's nebula of participants legitimate, because creating many identities yields no advantage over one bonded, peer-verified agent. From Agent0021's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
